title: the DSG Deepearth areas 24-25
audit_comment: The DSG Deepearth areas 24-25 pin Area 24 (the Domain of the Duergar with its hundred caves, dammed reservoirs, slave mines, gold sculptors and fungus breweries) and Area 25 (the Windpipe with its six living caves, the drow outpost, and the alternating-blast shaft to the mountain crevasse).

banner.title: THE DSG DEEPEARTH AREAS 24-25, R545: printed p. 94 (pdf 95) - the individual area key crosses the gray dwarf domain and the shaft: Area 24 the Domain of the Duergar (the largest concentration of gray dwarves in Deepearth, nearly a hundred natural caves widened and stairwayed; the living caves with their plentiful flowing water, the water-filled chambers with ledged walkways, the drought-proof dammed reservoirs; the central council cavern; the 30-foot navigable outflow stream with its dry walkway; the 8,000 duergar with their rothe herds; the second-class derro tenants under protection; the hundreds of demoralized slaves - humans, goblins, svirfneblin, drow - with a 25% escape-join chance; the un-eradicable giant bats; the Grand Canyon air and the cut air ducts; the southwestern slave-worked mines of iron, copper and gold; the fine-art metal-working and the gold sculptors - 1d6 x 100 gp of statuary per residence, six times that in the larger homes, 2d6 x 1,000 gp in the council chambers and inns, life-size 20,000-gp statues in the largest chamber, each worth 1d4 + 1 times its gold intact on the surface; and the red-fungus breweries with their pungent potent ale and the one-or-two inns per cavern), and Area 25 the Windpipe (the six living caves with spectacular formations joining at the excavated chamber, each with an 80-foot, miles-long central room; the high-level drow outpost - 4th-or-higher fighters with a 5th-or-higher magic-user and cleric - patrolling and slaving; the doombats, piercers, oozes, jellies, slimes, lichens, basidironds, rats and crawlers; the 50% polluted pools with one or two pure sources per cave; and the shaft itself - about 20 feet wide, 20 miles to the mountain crevasse, door-sized entry, alternating blasts: one turn per hour roaring upward to ride lying down, four turns inactive, one turn down, timing varying as much as 50%; the journey five rounds up to Area 28 and eight down, the failed Intelligence Check halting a descent for 6d6 of falling damage).
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~12082-12255) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (capture idx 214 = the printed p. 94 window carrying Area 24 in full and the Area 25 head, idx 216 head = the printed p. 95 window carrying the windpipe body); the compiled-tables appendix has no reprint of this prose. A CLEAN-READ ROUND: both machine reads agree on every load-bearing number - the hundred caves, the 30-ft outflow, the 8,000 duergar, the 25% slave chance, the 1d6x100/6x/2d6x1,000/20,000-gp/1d4+1 gold ladder, the six caves with 80-ft chambers, the 4th/5th-level drow, the 50% polluted pools, the 20-ft/20-mile shaft, the one-turn up/four-turn lull/one-turn down cycle at 50% variance, the five-and-eight-round journeys and the 6d6 fall; the only garbles settled cross-read (the capture ld6, 2d6, ld4+1 and ld12 for the djvu dice, the djvu realms-o!for the capture realms of). SEAMS: the R518 water travel (the navigable outflow and the drow waterways ahead), the Monster Manual denizens (the duergar, derro, drow, rothe, doombats, basidironds), the R521-R522 mining (the slave-worked iron-copper-gold), the PHB Intelligence Check, and the gold-value economy. A ZERO-FLIP ROUND: the pp. 75-98 Deepearth child remains open until the setting lands in full (the R527/R533-R544 precedent - the gap report is NOT in the git add). Nothing auto-credits.
banner.sentinel: A procedural-plus-prose round: no tables pin. The numbers pin as consts per the R508 convention - the cave count, the outflow width, the duergar population, the slave escape percentage, the gold-value ladder (residence dice-sides-multiplier, the larger-residence multiplier, the public dice-sides-multiplier, the statue value, the intact dice-sides-base triple), the windpipe cave count and chamber height, the drow fighter and caster levels, the pool pollution percentage and pure-source minimum, the shaft width and miles, the blast-cycle turns, the timing variance percentage, the journey rounds up and down, and the fall dice, with the 1d6x100, 2d6x1,000, 1d4+1 and 6d6 pinned as count-sides(-multiplier/base) const triples or pairs. The geography, denizens, resources and unique-features prose pins as bools for both areas. The water-travel/MM/mining/PHB seams are noted; the Deepearth child stays open; nothing auto-credits.

consts.name: dnanCaveCount
consts.comment: nearly a hundred caves make up the domain of the duergar.

consts.name: dnanOutflowWideFt
consts.comment: the stream in the outflow tunnel is about 30 feet wide and is navigable by small boats.

consts.name: dnanDuergarPop
consts.comment: the duergar, the main inhabitants of the area, number about 8,000.

consts.name: dnanSlaveEscapePct
consts.comment: there is a 25% chance that a given group of slaves might be persuaded to join in an escape attempt.

consts.name: dnanResGoldDice
consts.comment: an average duergar residence contains 1d6 x 100 gp worth of small statuary (the die count).

consts.name: dnanResGoldSides
consts.comment: the average residence statuary is 1d6 x 100 gp (the die sides).

consts.name: dnanResGoldMult
consts.comment: the average residence statuary is 1d6 x 100 gp (the multiplier).

consts.name: dnanLargeResMult
consts.comment: larger residences may have up to six times the average residence value.

consts.name: dnanPubGoldDice
consts.comment: in public areas such as the council chambers or inns, gold sculptures are worth 2d6 x 1,000 gp (the die count).

consts.name: dnanPubGoldSides
consts.comment: the public-area sculptures are worth 2d6 x 1,000 gp (the die sides).

consts.name: dnanPubGoldMult
consts.comment: the public-area sculptures are worth 2d6 x 1,000 gp (the multiplier).

consts.name: dnanStatueGp
consts.comment: the largest chamber holds life-size solid gold statues of many prominent figures from the race's past, each containing about 20,000 gp worth of gold.

consts.name: dnanIntactDice
consts.comment: a statue returned to the surface intact is worth 1d4 + 1 times its gold content (the die count).

consts.name: dnanIntactSides
consts.comment: the intact surface value is 1d4 + 1 times the gold content (the die sides).

consts.name: dnanIntactBase
consts.comment: the intact surface value is 1d4 + 1 times the gold content (the base).

consts.name: dnanWindCaves
consts.comment: the six caves leading to the windpipe are living caves with many spectacular formations.

consts.name: dnanWindChamberHtFt
consts.comment: each windpipe cave includes a vast central chamber 80 feet high or higher.

consts.name: dnanDrowFighterLvl
consts.comment: all dark elves encountered in the area are fighters of 4th level or higher.

consts.name: dnanDrowCasterLvl
consts.comment: the drow outpost includes a magic-user and a cleric of 5th level or higher.

consts.name: dnanPoolPollutePct
consts.comment: the pools are subject to infrequent flowage, and about 50% of them have been polluted by noxious creatures or their droppings.

consts.name: dnanPureSourcesMin
consts.comment: each of the six large caves has at least one or two sources of pure water (the minimum).

consts.name: dnanShaftWideFt
consts.comment: the windpipe is about 20 feet wide.

consts.name: dnanShaftMiles
consts.comment: the windpipe stretches to a high mountain crevasse some 20 miles distant.

consts.name: dnanUpBlastTurns
consts.comment: for approximately one turn per hour the windpipe fills the surrounding caverns with a roaring sound as air blasts upward from the heart of Deepearth; during these spurts a character can step into the shaft, lie down, and be propelled upward, slowing or reversing his climb by changing orientation - a character standing upright falls at a rapid speed.

consts.name: dnanInactiveTurns
consts.comment: the windpipe is inactive for about four turns per hour, unsuitable for transportation.

consts.name: dnanDownBlastTurns
consts.comment: the windpipe carries a downward blast of air for another turn per hour, also unsuitable for transportation.

consts.name: dnanTimingVaryPct
consts.comment: the exact timing between blasts is a matter of guesswork and luck, since it varies as much as 50%.

consts.name: dnanJourneyUpRounds
consts.comment: the journey from Area 25 to Area 28 takes five rounds.

consts.name: dnanJourneyDownRounds
consts.comment: the reverse journey from Area 28 to Area 25 takes eight rounds, so bad timing - and fatalities - is not unheard of.

consts.name: dnanWindFallDice
consts.comment: failure to halt downward movement in the windpipe results in falling damage of 6d6 points (the die count).

consts.name: dnanWindFallSides
consts.comment: the windpipe fall deals 6d6 damage (the die sides).

bools.name: dnanGrayDwarfHome
bools.comment: this large network of natural caverns is the home of the largest concentration of gray dwarves, or duergar, in Deepearth; the duergar have widened some passages and built stairways.

bools.name: dnanLivingCaves
bools.comment: these are living caves containing plentiful supplies of fresh, flowing water; several are almost completely water-filled, but even these have small air spaces near the top with ledged walkways so the gray dwarves can move through them.

bools.name: dnanDammedReservoirs
bools.comment: the caves have been dammed to control outflow so the dwarves maintain a large water supply even during periods of drought.

bools.name: dnanCentralCaverns
bools.comment: like the deep gnome caves, the duergar caves contain large central open areas with extensive networks of dungeons and tunnels excavated for living quarters along the sides, plus a large central cavern established as a council chamber.

bools.name: dnanOutflowWalk
bools.comment: the east tunnel serves as the outflow for most of the area's water; a dry walkway runs beside the stream, allowing unimpeded foot travel.

bools.name: dnanDerroTenants
bools.comment: in several small attached caves the gray dwarves allow small communities of derro to live - treated as second-class citizens, they tolerate the arrangement for the protection of the huge duergar population.

bools.name: dnanSlaveCaverns
bools.comment: hundreds of slaves are imprisoned in small, poorly-ventilated caverns among the dwellings - humans, goblins, svirfneblin and drow, demoralized and listless.

bools.name: dnanGiantBats
bools.comment: many giant bats live in ceiling niches of the duergar caverns; despite everything the duergar can do they remain, preying chiefly on rothe but seizing a duergar, derro or slave when the opportunity arises.

bools.name: dnanRotheHerds
bools.comment: like the svirfneblin, the gray dwarves maintain large herds of rothe.

bools.name: dnanAirDucts
bools.comment: proximity to the Grand Canyon insures an adequate air supply, and the duergar have cut many air ducts through the rocks to aid circulation; even in drought the reservoir caverns hold enough water to last the gray dwarves for several years.

bools.name: dnanSlaveMines
bools.comment: at the southwestern end of their domain the duergar run an ambitious mining operation - a three-dimensional network of shafts and tunnels extending many miles, worked almost exclusively by slaves.

bools.name: dnanIronCopperGold
bools.comment: the duergar mine iron, copper and gold.

bools.name: dnanGoldSculptors
bools.comment: duergar metal-working is a fine art - tools, weapons and armor of the highest quality; gold is not used for such mundane purposes, but a cadre of highly skilled sculptors casts pure molten gold from stone models and molds into exquisite statuary.

bools.name: dnanFungusBrew
bools.comment: duergar breweries use a red fungus rather than grain, producing a pungent and potent ale common among the gray dwarves; each cavern has at least one or two side caves hollowed out as inns, well-attended at all times, and like the deep gnomes the duergar trade their products with neighboring cultures.

bools.name: dnanWindRoutes
bools.comment: several large caverns provide alternative routes through this area, joining at their northern extremities into the huge excavated chamber that contains the windpipe.

bools.name: dnanMilesLongCham
bools.comment: the central chambers of the windpipe caves run several miles long, linked by much narrower connecting passages to the excavated tunnel to Area 26 and the circular windpipe chamber.

bools.name: dnanDrowOutpost
bools.comment: a large outpost of drow lives in the windpipe chamber, and dark elf patrols are common in the connecting caves; because the windpipe allows access to their realms below, the outpost drow are of high level and morale, and they take prisoners as slaves from parties they can easily overpower.

bools.name: dnanWindFauna
bools.comment: despite the drow patrols the caverns host doombats and piercers among the ceiling stalactites, oozes, jellies and slimes among the small pools, lichen clusters on the floors, basidironds among harmless fungus, and giant rats and carrion crawlers moving restlessly cave to cave.

bools.name: dnanWindShaft
bools.comment: the windpipe is a smooth shaft through the earth stretching from the lowest realms of Deepearth to a high mountain crevasse; it accounts for most of the ventilation of the drow realms and also serves as a means of transportation, its entry in Area 25 a door-sized opening in the side of the shaft.

bools.name: dnanAlternatingBlasts
bools.comment: the windpipe is subject to alternating blasts of air that blow up from the depths and then back down.

bools.name: dnanWindSkill
bools.comment: the drow have become skilled at using the airflow between Areas 28 and 25; characters new to the experience must make successful Intelligence Checks to stop correctly - for upward travelers failure simply means reversing course.
